newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower on improving crop outlook.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower on improving crop outlook.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower as favorable crop weather in the United States, Europe and Australia and bearish technicals weighed on the market, floor sources said.

"We've got additional moisture and the threat of more moisture not only in France but also in Australia," one floor trader said, noting favorable planting weather in the U.S. spring wheat belt also helped to depress values.

Dealers said there continued to be talk that freeze damage in the U.S. hard red winter wheat areas during the weekend of April 12-13 may have been less severe that first believed. They noted the market had largely lost its "frost premium."
A tour of Kansas wheat fields this week organized by the Wheat Quality Council should give further indications on the extent of any damage.

July wheat closed at $4.31-1/2 a bushel, down 11 cents on the day and only 6-1/2 cents higher than its settlement on Friday April 11, prior to the weekend freeze. Two weeks ago July climbed as high as $4.98-1/2.
Other months on Monday closed 12 to two cents lower.
